I Moved to Linux and Its Even Better Than I Expected

This is how I feel.

I have a Windows machine (for work/school) and a MacBook for debugging things (I like to help people with problems), and I HATE both systems.

Windows is Windows... I don't think I have to explain that any further.

OSX is actually really interesting. It's familiar, and a lot of the things I do in Linux are the same, but it feel claustrophobic. I'm so used to being able to change anything and everything... Tweaking a setting or option I don't like until it does what I want... But you can't do that in OSX. Sure, there's a few choice things you can change, but it's NOTHING like in Linux... Hell, if I want an entirely different desktop environment, I can do that... But you can't even tweak the taskbar on OSX.

I've always thought the big hurdle in getting users to switch is that they don't know what they're missing.

Don't like your min/max/close buttons in that particular corner? Move them! Or get rid of them completely!

Don't like the background behind the text under your icons on your desktop? Get rid of it! Change the color! Make it an outline! Turn it into an animation!

The catch-22 is that, when you explain the freedoms you can have, it becomes intimidating to the average non-open-source user. Why would they NEED to move window buttons? What's wrong with text backgrounds? Why would I want to change the taskbar?

But everyone I've converted agrees that the "other" platforms feel claustrophobic.

I usually just show people screenshots of my system (mint 17 cinnamon with a minimalist gray and orange theme) and my wifes (also mint, but with pink and blue and translucent windows). That usually makes people curious.
